title: The head still has its own estimate from earlier today
replays: The 15 Nov 2026 class: on a food day the 85,000 B wire guard silently left out the head's own estimate and its comparison with the label, so 'Do you understand why?' got an answer without them. Synthetic busy food day of the same shape: the estimate was never logged, so only the conversation holds it.

texts: Daily targets: 1,900 kcal and 120 g protein; weekends may go to 2,100 kcal.
Log every meal and drink in the food ledger as soon as I report it, with kcal and protein per item.
For packaged food, use the label figures I give; ask for the pack size before estimating fruit or yogurt.
Round kcal to whole numbers and protein to one decimal place in replies.
Do not suggest skipping meals; suggest protein-led swaps instead.
I do not eat pork; flag it if a dish I describe usually contains it.
Coffee is always with whole milk unless I say oat milk or decaf.
My usual porridge is 60 g oats with 250 ml semi-skimmed milk.
My usual lunch wrap from the cafe downstairs is 540 kcal and 32 g protein per the label.
Weigh-ins are Monday mornings; remind me only if I ask about progress.
Keep replies short on weekdays: the logged line, the day total and what is left.
When I ask why an estimate was off, compare your estimate with the label figures item by item.
Gym days are Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday; on those days protein matters more than calories.
I am training for a 10 km run in March; long runs are on Sunday mornings.
Do not count black coffee, tea without milk or water as entries.
Treat a handful of nuts as 20 g unless I give a weight.
When a day goes over target, say so once, plainly, with no lecture.
Use metric units for food weights and millilitres for drinks.
The kids' leftovers I eat count as a snack entry with my best guess of the portion.
Remind me to drink water only if I ask for a daily review.
Bins go out on Tuesday night.
Water the ferns on Saturday morning.
The car service is due every 12 months, next in April.
Call my sister on Sunday evenings.
Back up the laptop on the first of each month.
The boiler service is due every October.
My dentist check-ups are every six months; the next is in January.
Order coffee beans when the bag is a quarter full.
The spare key is with the neighbor at number 4.
Replace the smoke alarm batteries each spring.
Do not book anything before 9 am on weekends.
Prefer trains over driving for trips to London.
My partner is vegetarian; suggest dinners we can share.
Pay the window cleaner on the last Friday of the month.
Recycling goes out on alternate Wednesdays.
The vet appointment for the cat is the first Monday of each month.
Check the plant food stock at the start of each season.
Renew the parking permit every January.
